title: Affine envelope and boundary criterion for a generalizing ringed subspace
statement:
Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine scheme for a commutative ring $A$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $H\subseteq|S|$ be stable under generalization, meaning that $s\in H$ and $s\in\overline{\{t\}}$ imply $t\in H$, and retrocompact, meaning that $H\cap U$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq S$. Give $E=S|_H=(H,\mathcal O_S|_H)$ the induced ringed-space structure [def-a1-ringed-subspace]. It is locally ringed [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Put $C=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_S|_H)$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and let $h:V\to S$ be induced by restriction $A\to C$. The morphism $k:E\to V$ is the canonical morphism whose map on global sections is $\mathrm{id}_C$. It identifies $E$ with the ringed subspace on its image $k(H)$, and $h\circ k$ is the canonical inclusion $E\to S$. One has $h^{-1}(H)=k(H)$. Write $B=h(|V|\setminus k(H))$. Then $E$ is a scheme if and only if $\overline B\cap H=\varnothing$; whenever $E$ is a scheme its canonical morphism to $S$ is a quasi-compact flat monomorphism [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Moreover $k$ is surjective if and only if it is an isomorphism, if and only if $E$ is an affine scheme.

For $s\in S$, put $S_s=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $H_s=c_s^{-1}(H)$, where $c_s:S_s\to S$ is the canonical local-spectrum morphism [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. The subset $H_s$ again satisfies the two hypotheses. Its induced ringed space $E_s=S_s|_{H_s}$ has canonical affine envelope $V_s$ as above. There is a canonical $S_s$-isomorphism $V_s\simeq V\times_S S_s$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Under this identification $k_s(H_s)$ is the inverse image of $k(H)$ and the image of its complement under $h_s:V_s\to S_s$ is $c_s^{-1}(B)$.

source.place: §2 Proposition 2.3(ii)–(iii), Proposition 2.4(A),(B) and Corollary 2.5(i),(ii), printed pp.4–8, specialized to affine S; boundary-image localization is the complement identification in the proof of Theorem 3.3, step 4°, printed p.13; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Since $S$ is affine, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], hence spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Retrocompactness applied to the quasi-compact open $S$ makes $H$ quasi-compact. The set of generalizations of $H$ is $H$ itself, by the hypothesis. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-generalizations-of-quasi-compact] expresses $H$ as the intersection of all quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of $H$. This is a nonempty set-indexed family (it contains $S$), closed under finite intersections by quasi-separatedness. Empty $H$ is allowed: the family then includes the empty open.

source.place: Tag 0A31, lemma-make-spectral-space, implication (3) to (4); Raynaud Lemma 2.1, printed p.4.

proof.text: Every quasi-compact open of the affine scheme $S$ is quasi-affine in the precise sense required by [lem-a1-intersection-canonical-affine-embedding]: it is already a quasi-compact open subscheme of $S$. Apply that node to the family in Step 1. It gives the locally ringed structure of $E$, the canonical $k:E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, and an identification of $E$ with the induced ringed subspace on $k(H)$. In particular this identification uses the actual sheaf map of $k$. By [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction], morphisms of locally ringed spaces into $\operatorname{Spec}A$ are determined by their maps $A\to\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)$. The maps for $h\circ k$ and the inclusion $i:E\to S$ are both restriction $A\to C$. Hence $h\circ k=i$.

source.place: Tag 0API, lemma-sits-in-functions, statement and proof; the affine adjunction is schemes.tex Tag 01I1.

proof.text: For use both at points and on principal opens, let $M\subset A$ be any multiplicative subset, $A'=M^{-1}A$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$, $c:S'\to S$, and $H'=c^{-1}H$. By [lem-sfb-localization-spectrum-flat-monomorphism], $c$ is flat. Every quasi-compact open $U\subset S$ is covered by finitely many principal opens $D(a_j)\subset U$, using the basis in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] and quasi-compactness. The contraction description in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] gives $c^{-1}D(a_j)=D(a_j/1)$. These are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Their finite union $c^{-1}U$ is quasi-compact. Thus the inverse images of the family in Step 1 are quasi-compact opens, closed under finite intersections, with intersection $H'$, and include $S'$. The affine scheme $S'$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-a1-qc-open-intersection-spectral-presentation] with member $S'$ and then [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral]. The projection $H'\hookrightarrow S'$ is spectral, so its inverse image of every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact: $H'$ is retrocompact. It is stable under generalization because it is an intersection of opens, and every open containing a point contains its generalizations. Taking $M=A\setminus\mathfrak p_s$ gives the two hypotheses for $H_s$.

source.place: Equation equation-sections-of-intersection preceding Tag 0APJ; Topology Tags 0A31 and 0A2Z; Algebra Tags 00E0 and 00E3 and Schemes Tag 01I3 for the finite principal-open cover. Raynaud Proposition 2.3(iii), pp.6–7.

proof.text: Put $E'=S'|_{H'}$ and $C'=\Gamma(H',\mathcal O_{S'}|_{H'})$. Apply [lem-a1-intersection-sections-flat-base-change] to $Y=S$ and the flat map $S'\to S$ from Step 3. Its hypotheses hold since $S$ is quasi-separated and $H$ is the nonempty-family intersection of Step 1. It gives the canonical isomorphism $C\otimes_A A'\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$, $u\otimes a'\mapsto c^\sharp(u)a'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its spectrum identifies $V'=\operatorname{Spec}C'$ with $V\times_SS'$, including both projections. The comparison on the induced ringed subspaces sends $H'$ to $H$ by $c$. Naturality of [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] identifies its composites with the canonical $k'$ and $k$: their section maps are exactly the restriction maps in the displayed tensor formula. Thus this is the canonical comparison of envelopes, with no scheme assumption on $E$. In particular it supplies the asserted $S_s$-isomorphism when $A'=A_{\mathfrak p_s}$.

source.place: Tag 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change; schemes.tex Tag 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affines. Raynaud Proposition 2.3(iii).

proof.text: For clarity about points in this base change, the tensor pushout [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] identify $C\otimes_A M^{-1}A$ with the localization of $C$ at the image of $M$. Indeed maps from either ring to any commutative ring $D$ are exactly maps $C\to D$ making every image of $m\in M$ a unit; the extensions agree on $C$ and $M^{-1}A$, so the two inverse comparison maps are forced. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] identifies the projection $\pi:V_s\to V$ with the embedding onto $h^{-1}(c_s(S_s))$: the condition on a prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ is that its contraction to $A$ be contained in $\mathfrak p_s$. Here [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] identifies $c_s(S_s)$ with the generalizations of $s$.

source.place: Tags 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization) and 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization); canonical local-spectrum description in schemes.tex.

proof.text: If $s\in H$, every generalization of $s$ belongs to $H$, so $H_s=S_s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. The ringed space $E_s$ is then $S_s$ and its global sections are $\mathcal O_{S,s}$; hence its envelope arrow $h_s:V_s\to S_s$ is an isomorphism by the affine-spectrum description [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Step 5 says every point of $V$ above $s$ lifts uniquely to $V_s$. Since $h_s$ is an isomorphism there is just one such point, and it is $k(s)$ by $h k=i$. Therefore $h^{-1}(H)=k(H)$. The argument applies to every affine pair satisfying the hypotheses, including $(S_s,H_s)$ of Step 3. It follows that $k_s(H_s)=h_s^{-1}(H_s)=\pi^{-1}(h^{-1}H)=\pi^{-1}(k(H))$. Finally Step 5 identifies $\pi$ with a bijection onto the points above the generalizations of $s$. For $t\in S_s$, a point above $t$ outside $k_s(H_s)$ exists exactly when a point above $c_s(t)$ outside $k(H)$ exists. Thus $h_s(V_s\setminus k_s(H_s))=c_s^{-1}(B)$, including equality of the stated boundary images.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization, applied after Steps 4–5; Raynaud Corollary 2.5(ii) and Theorem 3.3, proof 4°, printed p.13.

proof.text: Suppose first that $E$ is a scheme. Its canonical arrow $i:E\to S$ is flat: [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk] identifies each induced-sheaf stalk with $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and identifies the map of $i$ with that isomorphism, so it is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. It is quasi-compact since the inverse image of any affine open $W\subset S$ is the quasi-compact subspace $H\cap W$, by retrocompactness. It is monic as a ringed-space map. Two maps with equal composites have equal base maps since $H\hookrightarrow S$ is injective. For this fixed base map, a sheaf map from the inverse-image sheaf $i^{-1}\mathcal O_S$ is uniquely determined by its adjoint map from $\mathcal O_S$ under [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Equality of the composites says precisely that these latter maps are equal. Thus the maps into $E$ agree. All these claims concern the specified inclusion and its specified inverse-image sheaf [def-a1-ringed-subspace].

source.place: Tag 008H, lemma-stalk-pullback, and inverse-image adjunction; Raynaud Definition 1.4 and Proposition 2.4(A)(i),(ii).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-affine-neighbourhood] to $i$ from Step 7. Obtain an open $U\subset S$ containing $H$ such that $E\to U$ is affine. For each $s\in H$, choose $a\in A$ with $s\in D(a)\subset U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. The induced open $D(a)$ is affine with ring $A_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Its inverse image $E_a=E|_{H\cap D(a)}$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] applied to $E\to U$. Step 4 with $A'=A_a$ identifies its envelope with $V\times_SD(a)=h^{-1}D(a)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. Since $E_a$ is affine, its canonical map to its envelope is an isomorphism by [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Therefore $h^{-1}D(a)\subset k(H)$. Let $U_0$ be the union of these $D(a)$ for all $s\in H$. Then $H\subset U_0$ and $h^{-1}U_0\subset k(H)$, so $B\subset S\setminus U_0$. The latter is closed and avoids $H$; hence $\overline B\cap H=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0APJ (localization of sections) with schemes.tex Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine); Raynaud Proposition 1.5 and Proposition 2.4(A), necessity.

proof.text: Conversely assume $\overline B\cap H=\varnothing$ and put $U=S\setminus\overline B$. Then $k(H)\subset h^{-1}U$ since $hk=i$ and $H\subset U$. Every point of $V\setminus k(H)$ maps into $B\subset\overline B$, so $h^{-1}U\subset k(H)$. Thus $k(H)=h^{-1}U$ is open in $V$. Step 2 identifies $E$, with its actual sheaf, with the induced ringed subspace on this open; it is therefore the open subscheme of $V$, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. In particular $E$ is a scheme. Step 7 now gives all the asserted properties of its canonical morphism to $S$. This proves both implications of the boundary criterion.

source.place: Open-subspace description of open immersions (Tag 01HF); Raynaud Proposition 2.4(A), sufficiency.

proof.text: Step 2 already identifies $k$ with an isomorphism onto its induced ringed image. Hence if it is surjective, that image is all of $V$ and $k$ is an isomorphism. An isomorphism to $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ makes $E$ affine. Conversely if $E$ is affine, its canonical map $k$ is an isomorphism: for any presentation $E\simeq\operatorname{Spec}D$, the resulting isomorphism $C=\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)\simeq D$ induces an inverse by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the composite with $k$ is the identity by the section-map uniqueness of [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction]. Isomorphisms are surjective. This proves the three equivalences, also for the empty affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}0$.

source.place: Tags 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine) and 01I2 (lemma-category-affine-schemes); Raynaud Proposition 2.4(B) and Corollary 2.5(i).

The a1 embedding applies with Y=S (qc opens of an affine scheme are quasi-affine), and the affine adjunction gives hk=i. Retrocompactness of H' under any localization follows from the spectral presentation and directed-limit nodes. a1 flat base change gives V'=V×_S S'. C⊗M^{-1}A is a localization of C, so the projection is an embedding onto the points over the generalizations of s. From this, h^{-1}H=k(H) and the boundary-image localization follow pointwise. qc, flat and mono follow from the inverse-image adjunction and the stalk isomorphism. The Raynaud 1.5(i) node, the D(a) charts and Step 4 give closure(B)∩H=∅. The converse is an open-subscheme argument, and surjective ⇔ iso ⇔ affine follows from adjunction uniqueness. Small cases tested: punctured A^2, the generic point, the punctured local spectrum, height ≤1 points of A^2 (non-scheme, closure(B) meets H), and empty H.
